method: Independent mathematical analysis of actual official statements; no inaccessible editorial is claimed read.

reviews.statement_summary: Positive-weight undirected graph up to100000 vertices/edges; output a shortest1-to-n path or-1, including loops and parallel edges.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Use Dijkstra with64-bit distances and a parent per strict relaxation, then follow parents from n. Extracting the smallest unsettled distance is safe because weights are positive; ignore stale heap entries. O((N+M)logN). Check m=0, unreachable target, parallel edges and path reconstruction rather than printing only the distance.

reviews.statement_summary: Count reachable restaurant leaves in a rooted tree when the path may not contain more than m consecutive cat-marked vertices.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Traverse from root carrying consecutive-cat count: increment on cat, reset on non-cat, and prune above m. A root-to-leaf path is unique, so this state exactly captures its validity. Count childless non-root vertices only after the check. O(N); use an iterative stack for depth100000.

reviews.statement_summary: Choose friends maximizing nonnegative friendship-factor sum while their maximum-minus-minimum money difference is strictly below d.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Sort by money and use two pointers to keep max-min<d. Nonnegative factors mean including every friend within a valid money interval cannot hurt, so an optimum is represented by a contiguous sorted window. Maintain a64-bit sum; equality to d is forbidden. O(NlogN), including sorting.

reviews.statement_summary: A checkpost protects precisely mutually reachable junctions; minimize total cost, then number of posts, and count optimum choices modulo1e9+7.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Mutual reachability is exactly the SCC equivalence relation. Each SCC needs at least one post, and its cheapest vertex suffices. Sum component minima in64-bit; multiply counts of minima modulo1e9+7. The minimum-post tie-break still selects one vertex per SCC even when costs are zero. O(N+M).

reviews.statement_summary: A cycle-free manager forest with up to2000 employees; partition into minimum groups with no ancestor pair in a group.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: A longest manager chain forces at least its vertex count groups. Grouping employees by depth from any root attains that bound because ancestors have strictly smaller depth. Thus answer is maximum root-to-vertex depth. O(N) with parent/children traversal; support multiple roots and a singleton.

reviews.statement_summary: Given a tree and a permutation, decide whether some neighbor order makes BFS from1 output exactly that permutation.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Require first vertex1. Map each vertex to its proposed position, sort each adjacency list by that position, then run BFS and compare the whole output. Any feasible order must enqueue a parent's unseen children in proposed relative order, so this canonical order succeeds iff one exists. O(NlogN); same depth alone is insufficient.

reviews.statement_summary: From positive n reach positive m<=10000 by doubling or subtracting1, minimizing button presses; hitting0 is invalid.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: For n>=m, decrement directly is optimal. Otherwise BFS the implicit unweighted graph on positive states up to2m: an optimal path never needs to double a value already at least m, since that only adds unnecessary downward steps. Every valid operation is one edge, so BFS distance is minimal. O(n+m) state bound; exclude0.

reviews.statement_summary: Find an alphabet ordering that makes given names lexicographically sorted, or Impossible; all26 letters must appear in the output.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Adjacent names contribute a precedence edge only at their first differing character. If the earlier name strictly extends a later prefix, reject immediately. Topologically sort all26 letters, including unconstrained ones; a cycle means impossible. Adjacent comparisons suffice for total sortedness. Deduplicate edges or keep indegree multiplicity consistent.

reviews.statement_summary: Railway graph and complementary road graph share vertices; train and bus leave1 simultaneously and must avoid simultaneous intermediate meetings.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Exactly one network has the direct edge1-n. Send that vehicle directly to n in one hour; it never visits an intermediate vertex and may wait at n. BFS the other network, which dominates the final arrival time. Return-1 if that route is unreachable. O(N²) adjacency/complement scan is sufficient for N<=400.

reviews.statement_summary: Remove as many train routes from capital as possible while preserving every shortest distance in a positive-weight road/train graph; duplicate trains allowed.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Compute shortest distances with all trains. A city with a shortest incoming road needs no retained train; road predecessors strictly decrease distance, so they cannot form a dependency cycle. A non-capital city without such a road needs exactly one train attaining its distance. Keep one for each such city and remove all others, including duplicate equal trains.64-bit distances; O((N+M+K)logN).

reviews.statement_summary: Find a spanning tree maximizing its maximum vertex degree in a connected simple graph.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: No spanning-tree degree can exceed the graph's maximum degree Delta. Pick a maximum-degree vertex, include every incident edge first, mark/enqueue all its neighbors, then extend this star by BFS. Each discovery adds one new vertex, so no cycle forms and all vertices are reached. The chosen root attains Delta; O(N+M).

reviews.statement_summary: Find a spanning tree with degree exactly D at vertex1, or reject, in a connected simple graph.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Remove vertex1 and find remaining connected components. Need at least one chosen neighbor from each component, and cannot choose more than deg(1), so feasible iff componentCount<=D<=deg(1). Select one representative neighbor per component, add extra distinct neighbors until D, then multi-source BFS ignoring vertex1 to complete the forest. Attach all seeds to1; edge count/connectivity prove a tree. O(N+M).
